title: Lesson 12: Expanding Horizons — Quantum Computing Architecture — js-tools
desc: Classical bits against qubits, superposition, entanglement, the Hadamard/CNOT/Pauli gates, Shor and Grover, and Born-rule measurement. Verified with a separate engine: H on |0⟩ gives P(0)=P(1)=50%, and the Bell circuit produces real entanglement with P(00)=P(11)=50% and P(01)=P(10)=absolutely 0%. Also covers why NISQ falls short — at 0.1% error per gate, 100 gates succeed 90.48% of the time but 10,000 gates only 0.0045% — and the error-correction overhead: a surface code at d=25 costs 625 physical qubits per logical qubit, so breaking RSA-2048 needs 2,500,000 physical qubits. Plus the post-quantum answer, which runs on classical machines.
